Randburg Jacuzzi

By: Kate Barry | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We dive into Randburg's deepest pothole and fish for answers from the City of Joburg

Unique Selling Point:
Cape Town has early morning polar plunging into the sea, but here in Joburg we have our own natural spring. On the corner of Pretoria Avenue & Harley Street is a massive open-air jacuzzi. It’s free, easily accessible to everyone, with clean filtered, chlorinated water gushing out 24 hours a day.

It started life as a pothole about a few years ago and has been through various incarnations. I’ve seen waste pickers stuffing cardboard and bags of paper in there. Eventually the water leak surfaced and on Google maps you can track the development, from a steady trickle to a serious burst pipe.

Last Monday I actually filmed it - a huge clear pool with fresh water bubbling out, covering an entire lane. The water flows freely downhill, ironically straight past the COJ Customer Service Centre.

I tweeted about it last Monday - asking Joburg Water to please attend to the lap pool on the corner. Somebody tagged MMC Kenny Kunene - unfortunately he was otherwise occupied that afternoon. At the home of Katise Molefe. Nevertheless, Joburg Water responded and said they would sort it out.

This morning it has grown - the jacuzzi pool now cover 1.5 lanes, the water is deep and is clearly a hazard to pedestrians and motorists.
Joburg Water has just announced that they will bill customer separately to COJ. Why? Let’s take a look at what it would take to get this one burst pipe fixed. Who tried, who failed, what went wrong? Who is up to the task?
Put presenter in a costume and take a dip. Humorous, but serious topic, guaranteed to enrage and amuse.


Summary:
Last week we filmed it - a huge clear pool with fresh water bubbling out, covering an entire lane. The water flows freely downhill, ironically straight past the COJ Customer Service Centre in Harley Street.

I tweeted about it last Monday - asking Joburg Water to please attend to the lap pool on the corner. Somebody tagged MMC Kenny Kunene - unfortunately he was otherwise occupied that afternoon. At the home of murder suspect Katise Molefe. Nevertheless, Joburg Water responded and said they would sort it out.

A week later and it has grown - the jacuzzi/pool now cover 1.5 lanes, the water is deep and is clearly a hazard to pedestrians and motorists.
Joburg Water has just announced that they will bill customer separately to COJ. Why? Let’s take a look at what it would take to get this one burst pipe fixed. Who tried, who failed, what went wrong? Who is up to the task?


Further information:
MacFarlane will don a wetsuit, goggles and snorkel to get to the bottom of this problem. The President claimed to be shocked at the state of the City and read the riot act to Panyaza Lesufi and Dada Morero. But that hasn't helped except in Sandton where the G20 is expected to be held in November.

Script:


JOZI JACUZZI

Sfx: Alarm
4:23am

V/O: You may have heard of the 5:00am club – where high achievers get up at dawn to boost mental focus and reach peak performance. This is not a story about that.

Sfx: Bike crash

V/O: You may have heard of cold-water swimming, where Capetonians take to the icy waves, or elderly women go boogie boarding at sunrise.
This is not a story about that either.

Sfx: Wave wipeout

Link: As a swimmer when we’re training for Iron Man - especially in Joburg -we’re always looking for open water venues. I’ve found one right in the middle of the city, in Randburg. here in Randburg. So those guys in the Cape can keep their beaches and their tidal pools. Here we have the Jozi Jacuzzi. Let’s go.

Oh, it’s cold! It’s pretty cold. So, it’s like some of the venues that we swam at. Oh, but it’s cold! Haha! At least I can still float.

V/O: The Jozi Jacuzzi started life as a little leak. Back in 2010 this corner seemed fine, but over the years things deteriorated. In 2017 there’s clearly a problem - but now this could be the source of the Nile.

Lucinda: You must understand that this is causing the water pressure to be lower in many of the households around here. And not just for like a week, but like six months.

V/O: Lucinda Harman is the councillor for Ward 102. She’s been making waves about this all year.

Lucinda: They come with this massive TLB. They’re all over the place and they rip and they, you know, create more and more of a crater. And every time they tried to fix it, they worsened it.

V/O; This is what the jacuzzi looked like in April. In May Johannesburg Water arrived with a TLB to fix it. In July the Tractor Loader Backhoe was back - being used to scoop water out of the hole.

Link: So how did things get so bad? What you see bubbling up here at a rate of… I don’t know, a million litres per minute, is just a drop in the ocean compared to the water that’s been wasted over the months. So, who should have fixed it? Joburg Water or the Johannesburg Roads Agency? Talk about the devil and the deep blue sea!

Lucinda: They keep telling me they’re getting to it, they’re getting to it, and they’re trying to find materials, and they’re trying to find the right Purchase Order number. Purchase Order for what? I still don’t know because the Purchase order number comes when it’s time for JRA to come and do the reinstatement. And until they fix the burst, JRA can’t even do a reinstatement, so it looks like it’s just stalling tactics right now.

V/O: So where is all the water going? Just a block downhill is another hidden gem: here at the confluence of Harley Street and Oak Avenue you will find the Ferndale Potholes, a natural geological formation that mysteriously fills with water even in the dry season. It’s fast becoming a favourite for nature lovers and motorists alike.

Lucinda: I mean, a Porsche went in there last weekend.

V/O: But just a dozen water leaks away from here is the jewel in the crown of Randburg’s pothole portfolio - Kenny’s Canyon or Kenny se Gat, named after MMC Kenny Kunene, the former Member of the Mayoral Committee for Transport. The hole has become a cultural landmark, reminding visitors to the adjacent hotel and shopping centre of the city’s mining heritage.

Francois: We haven’t found diamonds or oil yet, but it’s been here for just over a year.

V/O: Francois du Buisson is the mine manager of Ferndale on Republic.

Francois: It started off as a routine standard water leak, and Joburg Water dug and dug and dug and dug and didn’t find the leak, and they kept on digging a little bit more. Then we had to like, dig a lot more. They had to dump the sand on my incoming lane into the mall.
And they got to a point where they eventually then found the leak, and everybody was extremely excited.

V/O: Joburg Water may have fixed the leak, but they also dug up the stormwater drains, the fibre cables, the power cables and everything in between. And so, an 8-metre-deep hole was left standing for over a year.

Mac: So, Francois, has there been any incidents here as a result of this hole?

Francois: Well, Macfarlane, we’ve been very lucky. I mean at landlord’s expense we put up the contractor’s barrier net.

V/O: But one shopper almost lost her brand-new car.

Francois: She turned right to drive into the centre. So, my cleaner was walking across the road. The lady had a bit of a skrik. She bumped her and ended up halfway in the hole.

James: It’s a hazard; people stop wanting to come here. Everybody around here has their livelihoods threatened, basically degraded, because the City cannot do the basics of fixing infrastructure.

V/O: Member of Parliament James Lorimer joined the DA’s party to mark the one-year anniversary of the hole.

SFX: Happy birthday Kenny’s hole, a year gone by still no control.

James: We had a birthday cake; we had a banner; we named the hole Kenny’s Canyon – or less politely, Kenny se Gat – and it got tremendous response on social media.

V/O: Even Chester Missing got in on the act.

Chester: There’s a massive hole in a street in Joburg that’s 2-storeys deep, that’s been sitting there for 2 years. So well done to the DA that are celebrating its birthday party and calling it Kenny se gat. Which is a stupid name ‘cos we all know that Kenny se gat is Gayton Mackenzie.

Mac: But whose responsibility is it to fix it?

James: In the end it’s a reinstatement of roads. So, it’s Joburg Roads Agency. They kick the bucket back to Joburg Water and various other people saying they haven’t done their job. But frankly, as residents of Joburg, it’s not our problem. It’s their problem. They must sort it out. Don’t come to us with an excuse that lasts for more than year that. You can’t do your job, it’s unacceptable.

V/O: But this must seem like small fry compared to Lillian Ngoyi Street which has taken over two years to repair. Overseeing the Johannesburg Roads Agency at the time was MMC Kenny Kunene. The so-called Papa Action promised to propel the city into the future. But that voyage of discovery ended abruptly when police found him at the home of murder-accused Katiso Molefe. Kunene’s excuse? He was moonlighting as Editor of his online publication and mentoring a young journalist.

V/O: Too many holes in his story led to Kunene’s resignation. We reached out to him for comment on Randburg. But Papa Action didn’t respond.

Link: So, the man they call the Sushi King thought the public would swallow his excuses hook, line and sinker, but his explanation just didn’t hold water. It seems Kenny’s career has seen its gat and now that he’s resigned, he’s off the hook. We’ll have to fish for answers somewhere else.

V/O: So, we requested an interview with Joburg Water.

Mac: Not a fish.

V/O: But they didn’t bite. Perhaps they were too busy dealing with another massive pipe burst in Roosevelt Park.

JRA confirmed an interview with their CEO Zweli Nyathi, but two hours later they detoured, saying the City of Joburg should respond instead.

Mac: I’ve come into the city to see if I can get any answers whatsoever from the JRA. But with all the leaks happening in the city, I’m not taking any chances

V/O: We got our answers in writing. The JRA inspected Kenny’s se Gat in September last year, followed by a topographical and geotechnical survey in November, and a design and cost estimate for the repair. After Joburg Water finally accepted the quotation, they appointed a contractor to repair the hole on the 23rd of July.

Text: An investigation into the extent of the damage was conducted by the JRA in September 2024.
A topographical survey and a geotechnical survey were conducted in November 2024.
The JRA conducted a design and a cost estimate for the repair of the project.
Joburg Water furnished JRA with a Purchase Order.
The JRA appointed a contractor to address the full scope of the project on the 23rd of July in 2025

V/O: But Ferndale on Republic had to take the legal route to get things going. On the 3rd of June they applied for a court interdict to compel the JRA to repair the hole.

Francois: We got a court date for the 29th of July, which was last week Tuesday. We received correspondence from the City to say things are now going to happen.

V/O: And holy moly, during the interview the contractors arrived to begin fixing Kenny’s se Gat. The repairs will take 3 months.

V/O: Back at the Jozi Jacuzzi things were bubbling over, as the Municipality floated an explanation for why they haven’t been able to fix the leak. They need a new T-piece to replace the old T-piece.

Text: Repairs were undertaken; however, the water leak recurred. Joburg Water had to create a T-piece to replace the old T-piece.

V/O: Thankfully, I was out of my one-piece by the time the big fish arrived at the scene, Gauteng MEC for Agriculture, Vuyiswa Ramokgopa.

MEC: Well firstly it’s absolutely unacceptable. I’m hearing from the local residents that this particular hole where water is gushing out – litres and litres of water a day is gushing out – and it’s been like this for two years.

V/O: Ironically, Rise Mzansi is part of the coalition that governs Gauteng.

MEC: So, from where I’m sitting it’s just another testament to the dysfunction that has beset Joburg and the complete decay of Joburg.

V/O: On a surprise visit to the metro in March, President Ramaphosa said the same.

President: I found the city filthy. The city was not clean. There was rubbish all over the show, that experience wasn’t very pleasing. (March 2025)

V/O: Not a good look ahead of the G20 summit, which will be attended by various world leaders.

Lesufi: I apologise to the President that he had that particular experience.

V/O: Premier Lesufi apologised to the President, but not to the people of Johannesburg. Mayor Morero then made promises.

Morero: From now watch this space. We will not disappoint you any further. As the people of Johannesburg, we are ready to host the G20 Summit. It is not true that we are only providing services because of the G20.

V/O: But it is Sandton, not Randburg that is enjoying a facelift in preparation for the G20 summit.

Link 4: The mayor seems out of his depth when it comes to finding solutions. But relax, Sandton may be benefiting from the G20, over here in Randburg we have the G&T20.

V/O: Last week Joburg Water finally got their ducks in a row and began work on the Jozi Jacuzzi. But even the new T-Piece couldn’t solve the problem. They say repairs will be completed this week, even if it means running an extension cord from the local barber across the road.
But with municipal elections around the corner, some officials might find themselves up the creek without a paddle.

Show: Title Author Last Updated 17 August 2025 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 17 August 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: JOZI JACUZZI Sfx: Alarm 4:23am V/O: You may have heard of the 5:00am club – where high achievers get up at dawn to boost mental focus and reach peak performance. This is not a story about that. Sfx: Bike crash V/O: You may have heard of cold-water swimming, where Capetonians take to the icy waves, or elderly women go boogie boarding at sunrise. This is not a story about that either. Sfx: Wave wipeout Link: As a swimmer when we’re training for Iron Man - especially in Joburg -we’re always looking for open water venues. I’ve found one right in the middle of the city, in Randburg. here in Randburg. So those guys in the Cape can keep their beaches and their tidal pools. Here we have the Jozi Jacuzzi. Let’s go. Oh, it’s cold! It’s pretty cold. So, it’s like some of the venues that we swam at. Oh, but it’s cold! Haha! At least I can still float. V/O: The Jozi Jacuzzi started life as a little leak. Back in 2010 this corner seemed fine, but over the years things deteriorated. In 2017 there’s clearly a problem - but now this could be the source of the Nile. Lucinda: You must understand that this is causing the water pressure to be lower in many of the households around here. And not just for like a week, but like six months. V/O: Lucinda Harman is the councillor for Ward 102. She’s been making waves about this all year. Lucinda: They come with this massive TLB. They’re all over the place and they rip and they, you know, create more and more of a crater. And every time they tried to fix it, they worsened it. V/O; This is what the jacuzzi looked like in April. In May Johannesburg Water arrived with a TLB to fix it. In July the Tractor Loader Backhoe was back - being used to scoop water out of the hole. Link: So how did things get so bad? What you see bubbling up here at a rate of… I don’t know, a million litres per minute, is just a drop in the ocean compared to the water that’s been wasted over the months. So, who should have fixed it? Joburg Water or the Johannesburg Roads Agency? Talk about the devil and the deep blue sea! Lucinda: They keep telling me they’re getting to it, they’re getting to it, and they’re trying to find materials, and they’re trying to find the right Purchase Order number. Purchase Order for what? I still don’t know because the Purchase order number comes when it’s time for JRA to come and do the reinstatement. And until they fix the burst, JRA can’t even do a reinstatement, so it looks like it’s just stalling tactics right now. V/O: So where is all the water going? Just a block downhill is another hidden gem: here at the confluence of Harley Street and Oak Avenue you will find the Ferndale Potholes, a natural geological formation that mysteriously fills with water even in the dry season. It’s fast becoming a favourite for nature lovers and motorists alike. Lucinda: I mean, a Porsche went in there last weekend. V/O: But just a dozen water leaks away from here is the jewel in the crown of Randburg’s pothole portfolio - Kenny’s Canyon or Kenny se Gat, named after MMC Kenny Kunene, the former Member of the Mayoral Committee for Transport. The hole has become a cultural landmark, reminding visitors to the adjacent hotel and shopping centre of the city’s mining heritage. Francois: We haven’t found diamonds or oil yet, but it’s been here for just over a year. V/O: Francois du Buisson is the mine manager of Ferndale on Republic. Francois: It started off as a routine standard water leak, and Joburg Water dug and dug and dug and dug and didn’t find the leak, and they kept on digging a little bit more. Then we had to like, dig a lot more. They had to dump the sand on my incoming lane into the mall. And they got to a point where they eventually then found the leak, and everybody was extremely excited. V/O: Joburg Water may have fixed the leak, but they also dug up the stormwater drains, the fibre cables, the power cables and everything in between. And so, an 8-metre-deep hole was left standing for over a year. Mac: So, Francois, has there been any incidents here as a result of this hole? Francois: Well, Macfarlane, we’ve been very lucky. I mean at landlord’s expense we put up the contractor’s barrier net. V/O: But one shopper almost lost her brand-new car. Francois: She turned right to drive into the centre. So, my cleaner was walking across the road. The lady had a bit of a skrik. She bumped her and ended up halfway in the hole. James: It’s a hazard; people stop wanting to come here. Everybody around here has their livelihoods threatened, basically degraded, because the City cannot do the basics of fixing infrastructure. V/O: Member of Parliament James Lorimer joined the DA’s party to mark the one-year anniversary of the hole. SFX: Happy birthday Kenny’s hole, a year gone by still no control. James: We had a birthday cake; we had a banner; we named the hole Kenny’s Canyon – or less politely, Kenny se Gat – and it got tremendous response on social media. V/O: Even Chester Missing got in on the act. Chester: There’s a massive hole in a street in Joburg that’s 2-storeys deep, that’s been sitting there for 2 years. So well done to the DA that are celebrating its birthday party and calling it Kenny se gat. Which is a stupid name ‘cos we all know that Kenny se gat is Gayton Mackenzie. Mac: But whose responsibility is it to fix it? James: In the end it’s a reinstatement of roads. So, it’s Joburg Roads Agency. They kick the bucket back to Joburg Water and various other people saying they haven’t done their job. But frankly, as residents of Joburg, it’s not our problem. It’s their problem. They must sort it out. Don’t come to us with an excuse that lasts for more than year that. You can’t do your job, it’s unacceptable. V/O: But this must seem like small fry compared to Lillian Ngoyi Street which has taken over two years to repair. Overseeing the Johannesburg Roads Agency at the time was MMC Kenny Kunene. The so-called Papa Action promised to propel the city into the future. But that voyage of discovery ended abruptly when police found him at the home of murder-accused Katiso Molefe. Kunene’s excuse? He was moonlighting as Editor of his online publication and mentoring a young journalist. V/O: Too many holes in his story led to Kunene’s resignation. We reached out to him for comment on Randburg. But Papa Action didn’t respond. Link: So, the man they call the Sushi King thought the public would swallow his excuses hook, line and sinker, but his explanation just didn’t hold water. It seems Kenny’s career has seen its gat and now that he’s resigned, he’s off the hook. We’ll have to fish for answers somewhere else. V/O: So, we requested an interview with Joburg Water. Mac: Not a fish. V/O: But they didn’t bite. Perhaps they were too busy dealing with another massive pipe burst in Roosevelt Park. JRA confirmed an interview with their CEO Zweli Nyathi, but two hours later they detoured, saying the City of Joburg should respond instead. Mac: I’ve come into the city to see if I can get any answers whatsoever from the JRA. But with all the leaks happening in the city, I’m not taking any chances V/O: We got our answers in writing. The JRA inspected Kenny’s se Gat in September last year, followed by a topographical and geotechnical survey in November, and a design and cost estimate for the repair. After Joburg Water finally accepted the quotation, they appointed a contractor to repair the hole on the 23rd of July. Text: An investigation into the extent of the damage was conducted by the JRA in September 2024. A topographical survey and a geotechnical survey were conducted in November 2024. The JRA conducted a design and a cost estimate for the repair of the project. Joburg Water furnished JRA with a Purchase Order. The JRA appointed a contractor to address the full scope of the project on the 23rd of July in 2025 V/O: But Ferndale on Republic had to take the legal route to get things going. On the 3rd of June they applied for a court interdict to compel the JRA to repair the hole. Francois: We got a court date for the 29th of July, which was last week Tuesday. We received correspondence from the City to say things are now going to happen. V/O: And holy moly, during the interview the contractors arrived to begin fixing Kenny’s se Gat. The repairs will take 3 months. V/O: Back at the Jozi Jacuzzi things were bubbling over, as the Municipality floated an explanation for why they haven’t been able to fix the leak. They need a new T-piece to replace the old T-piece. Text: Repairs were undertaken; however, the water leak recurred. Joburg Water had to create a T-piece to replace the old T-piece. V/O: Thankfully, I was out of my one-piece by the time the big fish arrived at the scene, Gauteng MEC for Agriculture, Vuyiswa Ramokgopa. MEC: Well firstly it’s absolutely unacceptable. I’m hearing from the local residents that this particular hole where water is gushing out – litres and litres of water a day is gushing out – and it’s been like this for two years. V/O: Ironically, Rise Mzansi is part of the coalition that governs Gauteng. MEC: So, from where I’m sitting it’s just another testament to the dysfunction that has beset Joburg and the complete decay of Joburg. V/O: On a surprise visit to the metro in March, President Ramaphosa said the same. President: I found the city filthy. The city was not clean. There was rubbish all over the show, that experience wasn’t very pleasing. (March 2025) V/O: Not a good look ahead of the G20 summit, which will be attended by various world leaders. Lesufi: I apologise to the President that he had that particular experience. V/O: Premier Lesufi apologised to the President, but not to the people of Johannesburg. Mayor Morero then made promises. Morero: From now watch this space. We will not disappoint you any further. As the people of Johannesburg, we are ready to host the G20 Summit. It is not true that we are only providing services because of the G20. V/O: But it is Sandton, not Randburg that is enjoying a facelift in preparation for the G20 summit. Link 4: The mayor seems out of his depth when it comes to finding solutions. But relax, Sandton may be benefiting from the G20, over here in Randburg we have the G&T20. V/O: Last week Joburg Water finally got their ducks in a row and began work on the Jozi Jacuzzi. But even the new T-Piece couldn’t solve the problem. They say repairs will be completed this week, even if it means running an extension cord from the local barber across the road. But with municipal elections around the corner, some officials might find themselves up the creek without a paddle.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We dive into Randburg's deepest pothole and fish for answers from the City of Joburg
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Cape Town has early morning polar plunging into the sea, but here in Joburg we have our own natural spring. On the corner of Pretoria Avenue & Harley Street is a massive open-air jacuzzi. It’s free, easily accessible to everyone, with clean filtered, chlorinated water gushing out 24 hours a day. It started life as a pothole about a few years ago and has been through various incarnations. I’ve seen waste pickers stuffing cardboard and bags of paper in there. Eventually the water leak surfaced and on Google maps you can track the development, from a steady trickle to a serious burst pipe. Last Monday I actually filmed it - a huge clear pool with fresh water bubbling out, covering an entire lane. The water flows freely downhill, ironically straight past the COJ Customer Service Centre. I tweeted about it last Monday - asking Joburg Water to please attend to the lap pool on the corner. Somebody tagged MMC Kenny Kunene - unfortunately he was otherwise occupied that afternoon. At the home of Katise Molefe. Nevertheless, Joburg Water responded and said they would sort it out. This morning it has grown - the jacuzzi pool now cover 1.5 lanes, the water is deep and is clearly a hazard to pedestrians and motorists. Joburg Water has just announced that they will bill customer separately to COJ. Why? Let’s take a look at what it would take to get this one burst pipe fixed. Who tried, who failed, what went wrong? Who is up to the task? Put presenter in a costume and take a dip. Humorous, but serious topic, guaranteed to enrage and amuse.

metadata.Further information: MacFarlane will don a wetsuit, goggles and snorkel to get to the bottom of this problem. The President claimed to be shocked at the state of the City and read the riot act to Panyaza Lesufi and Dada Morero. But that hasn't helped except in Sandton where the G20 is expected to be held in November.
